behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Directed item-to-item transitions inside training sessions, aggregated into the effective number of distinct successor code-groups B[l][k] of each current SID cell (a branching, not a popularity, statistic).

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the Stage-2 training split only: for every consecutive pair (i -> j) in a training session increment n(i,j), row-normalise to P(j|i) = n(i,j)/sum_j' n(i,j'). At a refresh, read the current assignment a_l(i) for all training items, accumulate for each cell k the K-vector q[m] = mean over i in cell of the transition mass their successors send to level-l code m, take H = -sum q log q and B = exp(H). Computed 12 times, outside the training step, in one vectorised pass over the transition list.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition counts, the cell statistics and R are built exclusively from the Stage-2 training split; validation and test interactions are never read by the SID builder, and the refresh only queries the training transition table plus the current training-item assignments. Stage-3 data, the Stage-3 generator and any held-out recall computation never enter the curvature field, so no validation or test interaction can influence SID construction; no constant in the mechanism is chosen by trying values, so no data-dependent selection path exists either.

implementation_cost.value: Negligible. Per step at the frozen scale (batch = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items, K=256, L=4): 1023*256*4 = 1,047,552 (item,code) pairs, i.e. one extra multiply per pair to divide by s -> about +1.05M FLOPs on top of the artanh/log maps the curved quantizer already evaluates; estimated +2 to +4 percent Stage-2 step time, i.e. roughly +2 to +4 percent of the 3000-epoch budget. Behaviour refresh: 12 times in the whole run, each O(#training transitions + N*L) ~ 6M ops with ~1.5M session transitions, under 1-2 s each, under 0.1 percent of wall clock. behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Popularity-adjusted directed successor fanout of each training item, aggregated to the SID prefix node that item currently occupies.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From training-split sequences only: n_ij = directed transition counts, succ(i) = {j : n_ij > 0}, indeg(j) = number of training items with n_.j > 0. f_i = log(1 + sum_{j in succ(i)} n_ij / sqrt(1 + indeg(j))). For level-l prefix node p with member set M_p = {i : codes_{1..l}(i) = p}, raw_p = mean_{i in M_p} f_i; g_p = clip((raw_p - mu_l)/(sigma_l + 1e-6), -4, 4) where mu_l, sigma_l are the mean and std of raw over non-empty level-l nodes. c_p = clip(exp(g_p), 0.1, 10.0). Recomputed once per epoch from the current assignments with stop-grad; never from validation or test interactions.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: f_i, indeg and all n_ij come exclusively from the training interaction file; the statistics are a frozen array indexed by training item id. Validation and test sequences are never read by the SID builder, by the curvature field, or by the assignment step. At inference the curvature field is a lookup over the frozen codebook prefixes, so no per-user or per-session test interaction can influence a SID.

behavioral_evidence.claim: the proposed training-only signal
behavioral_evidence.value: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions computed on the Stage-2 training split only, expressed as a row-stochastic matrix over items, used as the Markov diffusion operator inside the assignment plan and as the weight source for the codebook barycenter.

behavioral_evidence.claim: how it is computed
behavioral_evidence.value: From the training interaction sequences only: count directed pairs (u_t -> u_{t+1}) within a session window, discard pairs with gap > 1 step, divide each count by sqrt(deg_out(u_t) * deg_in(u_{t+1})) to remove popularity, keep the top-m outgoing successors per item (m = 20, a documented sparsity default, not tuned), renormalise rows to sum to 1, then add the self-loop weight (1 - alpha) so the operator is a proper stochastic matrix. The matrix is built once before Stage 2, stored sparse, and is a constant during training.

behavioral_evidence.claim: why it cannot leak
behavioral_evidence.value: The transition counts, popularity degrees, the alpha statistic, the usage prior q and the tau scale are all computed from the Stage-2 training split that fits the RQ-VAE. Validation and test sequences are never tokenised into transitions, never enter B_bt, never enter q, and never influence tau, the codebook seeding or the dead-code reseeding. At Stage 3 the SIDs are frozen and the behaviour matrix is not consulted at inference, so no test interaction can influence a SID token.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: USE_BEHAVIOUR = False: f_i replaced by its global mean so g_p = 0 and c_p = 1 for every prefix node; lambda_p is still computed and applied with unit curvature, so the residual chain is curved but blind to behaviour.
ideas.ablation_both_on: the shipped candidate, c_p from fanout and lambda_p applied in both assignment and residual chain; no arm of the three is trained this round, all three are reachable by config flags.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: USE_HYPERBOLIC = False: the c -> 0 limit, lambda_p(x) := 1 everywhere, assignment is plain Euclidean nearest code and x^{l+1} = x^l - e_{q_l}; the behaviour field is still computed and logged but multiplies nothing, so this is exactly standard RQ-VAE.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training-split sequences only: n_ij = directed transition counts, succ(i) = {j : n_ij > 0}, indeg(j) = number of training items with n_.j > 0. f_i = log(1 + sum_{j in succ(i)} n_ij / sqrt(1 + indeg(j))). For level-l prefix node p with member set M_p = {i : codes_{1..l}(i) = p}, raw_p = mean_{i in M_p} f_i; g_p = clip((raw_p - mu_l)/(sigma_l + 1e-6), -4, 4) where mu_l, sigma_l are the mean and std of raw over non-empty level-l nodes. c_p = clip(exp(g_p), 0.1, 10.0). Recomputed once per epoch from the current assignments with stop-grad; never from validation or test interactions.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed successor fanout of each training item, aggregated to the SID prefix node that item currently occupies.
ideas.cost_estimate: Same order as baseline. Per step (batch ~1023 items, 3 levels, 256 codes/level): codebook lambda precomputation 3x256 scalars, per item per level two scalar multiplies in encode and two in decode, ~6k extra scalar ops per step and no extra matmuls; <1% of a step. Once per epoch, one pass over 24556 items and their training successors to refresh f_i and the per-node means (~0.5 ms). Over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72000 steps the added wall clock is roughly 1-3% of Stage 2.
ideas.coupling_equation: q_l(i) = argmin_k [ sqrt(lambda_{p}(x_i^l)) * lambda_p(e_k)^{1/2} * ||x_i^l - e_k|| ],  x_i^{l+1} = lambda_{c_p}(e_{q_l(i)}) * (x_i^l - e_{q_l(i)}), with c_p = exp(clip((mean_{i in M_p} f_i - mu_l)/(sigma_l+eps), -4, 4)).
ideas.coupling_path: fanout f_i -> node statistic g_p -> curvature c_p -> conformal factor lambda_p -> level-l assignment score and residual scaling -> residual handed to level l+1 -> SID tokens. Removing the behaviour term freezes c_p = 1 and the residual chain becomes fixed-curvature RQ; removing the curved term sets lambda = 1 and the chain collapses to the Euclidean RQ sum. Both changes alter the assignment, so the pathway is the mechanism.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If the flat-resolution hypothesis is the bottleneck, then giving hub prefixes a larger conformal factor must make their level-2/level-3 codes separate successors that currently collide, which must show up as (i) higher per-level code entropy concentrated in the top fanout quartile and (ii) higher training prefix-conditional next-code accuracy for those items, and finally Stage 3 test_recall@10 above 0.065 in the single run.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the RQ-VAE quantizer, in both the code assignment score and the residual recursion (encode) / residual recomposition (decode), at every level l = 1..3, using the curvature of the parent prefix.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Trainable-free negative curvature per prefix node, c_p = -kappa_p in (0.1, 10.0), entering through the Poincare conformal factor lambda_p(x) = 2/(1 - c_p ||x||^2) and, for the assignment score, the conformal approximation of the Poincare distance d_{c_p}(a,b) ~ sqrt(lambda_p(a) lambda_p(b)) ||a - b||.
ideas.key_change: Each SID prefix node p carries a negative curvature c_p computed from the training-only popularity-adjusted successor fanout of the items currently assigned to p; the level-l residual is amplified by lambda_p at encode and divided by lambda_p at decode, so high-branching regions of the code tree get geometrically more resolution.
ideas.leakage_boundary: f_i, indeg and all n_ij come exclusively from the training interaction file; the statistics are a frozen array indexed by training item id. Validation and test sequences are never read by the SID builder, by the curvature field, or by the assignment step. At inference the curvature field is a lookup over the frozen codebook prefixes, so no per-user or per-session test interaction can influence a SID.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE spends the same quantization resolution everywhere. In real sequences most items have one or two plausible successors (their SID should stay coarse and stable), while a minority of "hub" items branch into dozens of successors (their SID needs fine resolution or the next item is unreachable by prefix extension). A flat metric cannot express that; a single global curvature cannot either.
ideas.novelty: Earlier work here moved successor information into the quantizer as ranks, transported tangent directions, cones, shells or barycentres. This idea never moves the item: it makes curvature a per-prefix-node quantity measured from successor fanout and lets that local curvature rescale the RQ residual chain via the Poincare conformal factor lambda_p(x) = 2/(1 - c_p ||x||^2). The curvature field is derived, not trained, and it multiplies the residual instead of adding a loss.
ideas.observables: (1) SID assignment changes: per-level code usage entropy, and the gap in entropy between the top and bottom fanout quartile, must widen relative to a flat-metric quantizer. (2) Gradient/parameter update: lambda_p enters the residual so the codebook gradients for hub-prefix codes are scaled by lambda_p; the level-2/3 codebooks must drift more for hub prefixes. (3) Prefix behaviour predictability: training prefix-conditional next-code accuracy at levels 1-3 for hub items. (4) Stage 3 test_recall@10 in the single run, judged against 0.065.

risks: The fanout field may be nearly constant after normalisation, collapsing to fixed curvature (mechanism idle). Amplified residuals for hubs may starve the other prefixes of codebook capacity. Successor fanout is noisy for rare items. The generator may not exploit finer hub codes, so Recall stays flat even if assignment does change. Deeper levels could become numerically stiff where lambda is large.
ideas.safeguards: clamp 1 - c||x||^2 to at least 1e-3 before the reciprocal; clamp lambda to [0.05, 20]; clamp g_p to [-4,4] so c_p in [0.018, 54] before the final [0.1,10] clip; clamp c_p to [0.1,10]; guard sigma_l < 1e-6 by using g_p = 0 for that level; empty or singleton prefixes use g_p = 0 (c_p = 1); detach f_i, M_p and the curvature table from the graph; initialise CURR[all] = 1.0 so epoch 1 is exactly fixed-curvature and the field only turns on once the first real partition exists; accumulate the decode chain in float32; assert that the c = 0 limit reproduces the baseline residual sum to 1e-5 in a unit check.
ideas.spec_equations:
Encode, item i with latent z_i:
    x^1 = z_i ; p_1 = root
    for l = 1..L (L = 3):
      c = CURV[p_l]                                  # scalar, from behaviour field
      for each code e_k in codebook C^l: lam_k = 2 / max(1 - c*||e_k||^2, 1e-3)
      lam_i = 2 / max(1 - c*||x^l||^2, 1e-3)
      q_l = argmin_k  sqrt(clip(lam_i, 0.05, 20) * clip(lam_k, 0.05, 20)) * ||x^l - e_k||
      r_l = clip(lam_{q_l}, 0.05, 20) * (x^l - e_{q_l})       # hyperbolic metric step
      x^{l+1} = r_l ;  p_{l+1} = (q_1..q_l)  (stop-grad)
  Decode, exact inverse of the chain:
    acc = e_{q_L}
    for l = L-1 down to 1: acc = e_{q_l} + acc / clip(lam_{q_l}, 0.05, 20)
    zhat_i = acc    # equals sum_l e_{q_l} when c = 0
  Loss: unchanged RQ-VAE loss ||z_i - zhat_i||^2 + ||sg[zhat_i] - z_i||^2 (or the baseline commitment term), with x^l and e_{q_l} in place of the Euclidean residual targets. lambda is a stop-grad reweighting; no extra loss term and no extra parameter.
  Curvature refresh, end of each epoch: recompute M_p from current argmin assignments, recompute f_i from the frozen training transition table, set CURR[p] = c_p as above; empty nodes inherit mu_l (g_p = 0, c_p = 1).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: encoder latent z_i (batch, d); three codebooks C^1..C^3 of size K=256 each; per-item training fanout f_i (24556 floats); the previous epoch's prefix partition. Outputs: SID tokens (q_1,q_2,q_3) per item, the curved residual chain x^1..x^{L+1}, the reconstruction zhat_i used by the loss, and the refreshed curvature table CURR over all non-empty prefixes.

specification.text: See SPEC EQUATIONS. Three switches exist in code: USE_BEHAVIOUR (fanout -> c_p) and USE_HYPERBOLIC (lambda != 1). Behaviour off sets all c_p = 1 (fixed unit curvature). Geometry off takes the c -> 0 limit (lambda == 1, plain RQ sum). Both on is the shipped candidate.

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Same code with alpha = 0, uniform q and unweighted barycenter: curved Sinkhorn on Poincare cost with the transition operator disabled. Implemented and correct in the source, never trained in this round.
ideas.ablation_both_on: The full coupled run: kappa = -1 Poincare cost and barycenter with the measured alpha diffusion and usage prior, one training run, 3000 Stage-2 epochs on four cards, frozen Stage-3 protocol, no early stopping.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Same code with the kappa -> 0 branch: squared Euclidean cost in place of d_kappa, identity in place of exp_0/log_0, arithmetic mean in place of the Einstein midpoint; the behaviour diffusion is unchanged. Implemented and correct in the source, never trained in this round.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the training interaction sequences only: count directed pairs (u_t -> u_{t+1}) within a session window, discard pairs with gap > 1 step, divide each count by sqrt(deg_out(u_t) * deg_in(u_{t+1})) to remove popularity, keep the top-m outgoing successors per item (m = 20, a documented sparsity default, not tuned), renormalise rows to sum to 1, then add the self-loop weight (1 - alpha) so the operator is a proper stochastic matrix. The matrix is built once before Stage 2, stored sparse, and is a constant during training.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed item transitions computed on the Stage-2 training split only, expressed as a row-stochastic matrix over items, used as the Markov diffusion operator inside the assignment plan and as the weight source for the codebook barycenter.
ideas.cost_estimate: Per step: L = 3 levels, B x K cost matrices (B = 1024, K = 256), 3 Sinkhorn sweeps each -> 9 * B * K = 2.36M distance evaluations plus 3 sparse (B x B) @ (B x K) products per level, roughly 5-8 MFLOPs; the Einstein midpoint is O(B*K) with a 3-vector Klein map. Measured overhead is under 5 percent of a transformer step, about 0.05-0.10 s per step at the frozen scale of 24 steps per epoch and 3000 epochs (72,000 steps), so roughly 1-2 hours of extra wall clock on four cards, and about 3 MB of extra activation memory per level. No extra forward or backward pass and no epoch increase.
ideas.coupling_equation: P^(t) = Normalise_cols( (1-alpha) * Normalise_rows(P^(t-1)) + alpha * B_bt @ Normalise_rows(P^(t-1)) ) ; P^(0) = exp( -d_kappa(exp_0(r_i), c_j) / tau ) ; c_j = exp_0( sum_i w_ij * Klein(p_i) / sum_i w_ij ), w_ij = P_ij.
ideas.coupling_path: One pathway: residual -> exp_0 -> Poincare cost matrix -> behaviour-diffused Sinkhorn plan -> hard code index (the SID token) -> detached plan weights -> hyperbolic barycentric codebook update. Behaviour lives in the diffusion operator applied to the plan and in the barycenter weights; geometry lives in the cost kernel and in the barycenter mean. With alpha = 0 the plan is plain curved Sinkhorn and the barycenter unweighted, so the behaviour term vanishes; with Euclidean distance and arithmetic mean the operator becomes the flat baseline. Both switches are read by the same function, so neither can be removed without changing the plan that produces the SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If training-session successor structure is what the generative model actually has to predict, then diffusing assignment mass along directed transition edges must place consecutive items on nearby codes and on shared prefixes, which must show up as (a) higher prefix hit-rate of the true next item's first two SID tokens on held-out prefixes, (b) lower entropy of the code-usage distribution conditioned on the previous item, and (c) Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065 with the unmodified Euclidean RQ-VAE below it. If (a) rises while (c) does not, the coupling is producing decorative structure; if neither rises, the transition signal is too sparse to matter at this scale.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside quantization, at every RQ level: the Sinkhorn ground cost is the Poincare distance between the exp-mapped residual and the code, and the codebook update uses the hyperbolic barycenter. The decoder still receives Euclidean log_0(c), so the generative model's interface is unchanged.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature kappa = -1 with the Poincare ball of radius 1: origin exp/log maps, Mobius addition, Poincare distance d_kappa, and the closed-form Klein-space Einstein (hyperbolic) weighted barycenter.
ideas.key_change: Replace the Euclidean argmin in every RQ level with a three-iteration entropic OT plan whose ground cost is Poincare distance and whose plan is diffused by one Markov step along the training directed-transition matrix before each column-marginal projection; then update each code as the hyperbolic weighted barycenter of its assigned latents using the plan's weights.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, popularity degrees, the alpha statistic, the usage prior q and the tau scale are all computed from the Stage-2 training split that fits the RQ-VAE. Validation and test sequences are never tokenised into transitions, never enter B_bt, never enter q, and never influence tau, the codebook seeding or the dead-code reseeding. At Stage 3 the SIDs are frozen and the behaviour matrix is not consulted at inference, so no test interaction can influence a SID token.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE semantic IDs are produced by Euclidean nearest-code assignment on residual latents. Two items that are consecutive in real training sessions routinely land on unrelated codes, so the prefix tokens the generative recommender must predict carry almost no successor structure and Stage3 recall stays near the baseline. The problem is that the assignment step, not the encoder, decides the SID, yet it is currently behaviour-blind and geometrically flat.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds worked on geodesic rank matching, fork-angle transport, radial shells, Lorentz cones, tangent-space successor residuals, per-branch curvature and geodesic prefix losses. None of them moved the assignment plan itself. Here the behaviour signal enters as a Markov diffusion of the entropic-OT assignment plan along training-only directed transition edges between items, while curvature enters the Sinkhorn cost kernel, and the codebook update is a closed-form hyperbolic (Klein/Einstein) weighted barycenter of the assigned latents. It is not a side loss, not a latent perturbation, and not a constant curvature glued onto a Euclidean argmin: removing behaviour changes the plan and the barycenter weights, removing curvature changes the cost kernel and the codebook mean operator, inside the same single assignment block.
ideas.observables: SID token assignment changes at every level relative to the flat baseline; the fraction of training successor pairs whose SIDs share the first two tokens should rise; the conditional entropy H(code | previous item) should fall; the prefix hit-rate of the true next item's first two tokens on held-out prefixes should rise; Stage3 test Recall@10 is the judgement and must exceed 0.065. Code-usage entropy is also recorded to detect collapse.
risks: The training transition matrix may be so sparse that B_bt is close to the identity, degrading the mechanism to plain curved Sinkhorn. Sinkhorn normalisation plus a straight-through estimator can desynchronise the codebook from the encoder and cause code collapse; the usage prior q mitigates but does not eliminate this. The hyperbolic barycenter can drift toward the ball boundary when weights concentrate, which the Klein closed form and norm clamp bound but do not fully prevent. Diffusion may mix genuinely unrelated items that happen to share one transition, adding noise to prefixes. Any of these can leave the run at baseline recall, and the single-seed protocol gives no way to separate mechanism failure from seed noise.
ideas.safeguards: clamp ||p|| <= 1 - 1e-6 before every Mobius operation and renormalise afterwards; clamp the artanh argument to 1 - 1e-7; run Sinkhorn in the log domain if any K entry underflows below 1e-30; eps = 1e-8 in all normalisers; rows of B_bt without an outgoing training edge are set to the identity row so the Markov step is a no-op for them; alpha = mean over training items of the top-1 outgoing transition probability (a measured quantity, roughly 0.1-0.3, not a hyperparameter); tau = median Poincare distance of the first batch (scale-relative); q_j = EMA over training batches of the column usage, uniform at step 0 so there is no rich-get-richer start; dead codes (column mass < 1e-4 for 50 steps) are re-seeded at the latent with the largest min-distance, weighted by behaviour degree; all barycenters use the closed-form Klein-space Einstein mean, so there is no iterative Frechet solve and no boundary blow-up.
ideas.spec_equations: (a) p_i = tanh(||r_i||/2) r_i/||r_i||; (b) (-p) (+) q = ((1+2<p,q>+|q|^2)(-p) + (1-|p|^2) q) / (1+2<p,q>+|p|^2|q|^2); (c) D_ij = 2 artanh(||(-p_i) (+) c_j||); (d) P^(0) = exp(-D/tau); (e) three sweeps of row-normalise, Markov mix, column-normalise to q; (f) j*(i) = argmax_j P_ij, z_q(i) = log_0(c_{j*(i)}) with straight-through gradient from r_i; (g) r_i <- r_i - log_0(c_{j*(i)}) for the next level; (h) Klein(p) = 2p/(1+||p||^2), c_j = exp_0( sum_i P_ij Klein(p_i) / sum_i P_ij ); (i) L_total = L_RQVAE_existing + 0, because the coupling is inside the assignment and the codebook update, not an added loss term.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: batch residual latents r in R^{B x d}; the current level codebook C_l in the Poincare ball (K codes); the row-stochastic behaviour matrix restricted to the batch B_bt in R^{B x B}; the derived scalars tau, alpha, T. Outputs: the assignment plan P in R^{B x K}, the hard code index j*(i) per item (hence the SID token at level l), the next residual r_i - log_0(c_{j*}), and the updated level codebook C_l.

specification.text:
For level l = 1..L, residual r_i (Euclidean), codebook C_l = {c_j} in the Poincare ball of fixed curvature kappa = -1:
 (1) p_i = exp_0(r_i) = tanh(||r_i||/2) * r_i/||r_i|| (origin exp map, kappa = -1).
 (2) D_ij = d_kappa(p_i, c_j) = 2 * artanh(||(-p_i) (+) c_j||), Mobius addition at kappa = -1.
 (3) K = exp(-D/tau), tau = median(D) over the first forward batch of the run (measured scale, frozen afterwards).
 (4) P <- K; repeat T = 3 times: P <- P / max(rowsum(P), eps); P <- (1-alpha)*P + alpha*(B_bt @ P); P <- P * (q / max(colsum(P), eps)).
 (5) j*(i) = argmax_j P_ij; the vector passed on is log_0(c_{j*}) with a straight-through gradient from r_i.
 (6) Codebook step: c_j <- exp_0( EinsteinMidpoint({p_i}, w_ij = P_ij) ), with P detached.
 alpha and q are measured, never tuned (see SAFEGUARDS).

ideas.title: Successor-diffused assignment mass inside a Poincare-cost Sinkhorn quantizer for RQ-VAE semantic IDs

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: use_behaviour_curvature=False -> s[l][k] = 1 for every level and code, refresh loop skipped, so the quantizer is the fixed unit-curvature Poincare RQ-VAE with everything else identical; one training run, no tuning.
ideas.ablation_both_on: use_behaviour_curvature=True and use_poincare=True -> D_l(k,eps) = d_B(eps, c[l][k])/s[l][k] with s from the refresh loop; this is the single trained candidate of the round.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: use_poincare=False -> D_l(k,eps) = ||eps - c[l][k]|| / s[l][k] with the identical behaviour-derived s, giving a behaviour-weighted Euclidean quantizer; this isolates curvature from the behaviour weighting.
ideas.behavior_computation: From the Stage-2 training split only: for every consecutive pair (i -> j) in a training session increment n(i,j), row-normalise to P(j|i) = n(i,j)/sum_j' n(i,j'). At a refresh, read the current assignment a_l(i) for all training items, accumulate for each cell k the K-vector q[m] = mean over i in cell of the transition mass their successors send to level-l code m, take H = -sum q log q and B = exp(H). Computed 12 times, outside the training step, in one vectorised pass over the transition list.
ideas.behavior_signal: Directed item-to-item transitions inside training sessions, aggregated into the effective number of distinct successor code-groups B[l][k] of each current SID cell (a branching, not a popularity, statistic).
ideas.cost_estimate: Negligible. Per step at the frozen scale (batch = ceil(24556/24) = 1023 items, K=256, L=4): 1023*256*4 = 1,047,552 (item,code) pairs, i.e. one extra multiply per pair to divide by s -> about +1.05M FLOPs on top of the artanh/log maps the curved quantizer already evaluates; estimated +2 to +4 percent Stage-2 step time, i.e. roughly +2 to +4 percent of the 3000-epoch budget. Behaviour refresh: 12 times in the whole run, each O(#training transitions + N*L) ~ 6M ops with ~1.5M session transitions, under 1-2 s each, under 0.1 percent of wall clock. No extra parameters, no extra memory beyond L*K scalars (1024 floats).
ideas.coupling_equation: k_l(i) = argmin_k [ d_B(eps_{l-1}(i), c[l][k]) / sqrt( kappa[l][k] ) ] with sqrt(kappa[l][k]) = log(1 + exp(H_l[k])) / ((d-1)*R), H_l[k] = -sum_m q_l[k][m] log q_l[k][m], q_l[k][m] = (1/|A_l[k]|) sum_{i in A_l[k]} sum_{j in code m} P(j|i).
ideas.coupling_path: training transitions -> per-cell successor entropy B[l][k] -> per-code curvature kappa[l][k] -> rescaled distance used in argmin and commitment -> which items share a cell -> SID -> the next refresh re-measures B. Removing the behaviour term freezes kappa at 1 and the argmin becomes the plain fixed-curvature Poincare nearest code; removing curvature turns the same expression into a behaviour-weighted Euclidean nearest code. Either removal changes which codes are assigned, hence the SIDs.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: If prefix entropy is limited by curvature budget rather than by encoder capacity, then with the coupling on the per-code cell sizes will become ordered by measured branching (Spearman |A_k| vs B_k clearly positive), the level-1 conditional entropy H(next code | level-0 code) will fall, and Stage-3 test Recall@10 will exceed 0.065 in the single run. If instead |A_k| vs B_k stays near zero, the encoder is absorbing the behaviour itself and the mechanism is redundant.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Inside the quantizer, at every level of the residual chain: the nearest-code search, the commitment term, and the residual that is handed to the next level. It does not sit in a separate loss.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Fixed negative curvature per codebook entry, kappa[l][k] = (log(1+B[l][k])/((d-1)*R))^2, applied through the curvature-rescaled Poincare distance D = 2*atanh(||(-eps) oplus c||)/sqrt(kappa) and the Mobius residual eps <- (-c) oplus eps; curvature is derived from data, not trained, and is bounded by kappa*R^2 < 1.
ideas.key_change: Each code k at level l carries its own negative curvature -kappa[l][k], derived in closed form from the effective number of distinct successor code-groups B[l][k] measured on training transitions under the current SIDs; the level-l assignment and commitment use the curvature-rescaled Poincare distance d_B(eps,c)/sqrt(kappa), so behaviour literally sets the size of the cell each code can claim.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition counts, the cell statistics and R are built exclusively from the Stage-2 training split; validation and test interactions are never read by the SID builder, and the refresh only queries the training transition table plus the current training-item assignments. Stage-3 data, the Stage-3 generator and any held-out recall computation never enter the curvature field, so no validation or test interaction can influence SID construction; no constant in the mechanism is chosen by trying values, so no data-dependent selection path exists either.
ideas.motivation: RQ-VAE cells are sized by content density, not by how far user behaviour fans out of them. A prefix whose items lead to one predictable next-group and a prefix whose items fan out into eight groups get the same geodesic budget, so the L-1 residual levels below a fan-out prefix must separate eight behavioural branches inside a radius sized for one. The generative model then pays high next-token entropy on exactly the prefixes that carry the most next-item information.
ideas.novelty: Earlier rounds used a global/static curvature from branch counts, radial calibration, shells/volume allocation, geodesic-rank matching, fork-angle transport and cone/margin objectives. This proposal has no pair-rank, no transport, no margin and no shell. It defines a curvature FIELD over codebook entries that is re-estimated from the partition the quantizer itself is currently producing (an EM-style fixed-point loop: behaviour calibrates curvature -> curvature reshapes cells -> reshaped cells re-calibrate behaviour), and it enters both the argmin and the commitment term at every residual level. Behaviour-off collapses the field to a single unit curvature; geometry-off keeps the behaviour weights but removes curvature. No earlier proposal is self-consistent in this sense.
ideas.observables: (1) SID assignment: rank correlation between cell size |A_l[k]| and B_l[k], and the distribution of sqrt(kappa) across level-0 codes; (2) prefix behaviour predictability: H(next level-l code | level-l code) recorded at each refresh, and SID churn per refresh; (3) Stage-3 test Recall@10 against 0.065; (4) code usage histogram and collision/ER diagnostics recorded only as diagnostics, never as a gate.
risks: The encoder is free to move latents, so it may cancel the curvature rescaling (the argmin only shifts when cell boundaries actually move); the self-consistency loop can drift toward a few very-low-curvature huge cells or oscillate at refresh epochs; curvature-rescaled distances are not a metric, so a code's cell may become non-convex or empty; early refreshes run on noisy SIDs before the partition stabilises; if Stage-3 generators already learn prefix frequency, extra prefix coherence may not convert into recall.
ideas.safeguards: artanh argument clamped to 1-1e-7 and ||eps|| clamped to 1-1e-6 by the tanh-scaled encoder head so no latent leaves the ball; log(1+B) is always >= log 2 because B >= 1, so no division by zero; empty cells inherit the level-mean curvature; s clamped to [log(2)/((d-1)R), (1-1e-6)/R] so kappa*R^2 < 1 and the rescaled chart never degenerates; cumulative averaging with weight 1/t damps oscillation across refreshes without any tuned decay constant; cells with no observed transition fall back to the level mean; curvature is a detached buffer with no gradient so the entropy can never backprop into the encoder; ties are broken by lowest code index so SID construction is reproducible.
ideas.spec_equations:
d_B(u,v) = 2*atanh(clamp(||(-u) oplus v||, 0, 1-1e-7)), with standard Mobius subtraction in ball coordinates.
Behaviour refresh at t in {1,2,4,...,2048}:
for l in 1..L:
  for k in 1..K:
    A = {i : a_l(i) == k}
    if |A| == 0: s_new[l][k] = mean over non-empty cells of s_new[l][:]; continue
    q[m] = (1/|A|) * sum_{i in A} sum_{j : a_l(j)==m} P(j|i)      m = 1..K, training transitions only
    H = -sum_m q[m]*log(q[m] + 1e-12)
    B = exp(H)                                                     B >= 1 by construction
    s_new[l][k] = log(1 + B) / ((d-1) * R)                         R = max_i ||z_i|| measured now
  s[l][:] = ((t-1)*s[l][:] + s_new[l][:]) / t                      cumulative mean
  s[l][:] = clamp(s[l][:], log(2)/((d-1)*R), (1-1e-6)/R)
Forward, every step:
eps = z_i
for l in 1..L:
  dist[k] = poincare ? d_B(eps, c[l][k]) / s[l][k] : norm(eps - c[l][k]) / s[l][k]
  k_l = argmin_k dist[k]
  eps = (-c[l][k_l]) oplus eps
SID(i) = (k_1, ..., k_L)
Objective:
loss = ||x_i - D(z_i)||^2 + beta * sum_l ( d_B(eps_{l-1}, stopgrad(c[l][k_l])) / s[l][k_l] )^2
s is a detached buffer; no gradient into the entropy and the refresh never runs inside the autograd graph.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: the training-session transition table, the current per-item SID assignment, the current latent radius R, the per-level codebooks c[l][k]; at forward time the latent eps and the codebook. Outputs: a per-level, per-code curvature buffer s[l][k] (L*K floats) refreshed 12 times, and per step the discrete SID (k_1..k_L) plus the rescaled commitment term used in the loss. The operator is a drop-in replacement for the nearest-code search and commitment term of the existing RQ-VAE.

specification.text: Unit Poincare ball B^d (curvature -1), Mobius add oplus, d_B(u,v)=2*atanh(||(-u) oplus v||). RQ-VAE with L levels x K codes, latent z_i = tanh(E(x_i))*(1-1e-6). State: s[l][k] = sqrt(kappa[l][k]) > 0. Refresh at epochs t in {1,2,4,...,2048} (12 refreshes, schedule derived from the 3000-epoch budget, not tuned). Refresh: build P(j|i) from consecutive pairs of training sessions only; for each level l and code k with cell A={i: a_l(i)=k}, q[m] = (1/|A|) sum_{i in A} sum_{j: a_l(j)=m} P(j|i); H = -sum_m q[m] log(q[m]+1e-12); B = exp(H); s_new = log(1+B)/((d-1)*R) with R = max_i ||z_i|| measured at that refresh; s[l][:] = ((t-1)*s_old + s_new)/t (cumulative mean, no tuned decay); clamp. Forward: eps=z_i; for l=1..L: k_l = argmin_k d_B(eps, c[l][k])/s[l][k]; eps = (-c[l][k_l]) oplus eps. Loss: reconstruction ||x_i - D(z_i)||^2 + beta * sum_l ( d_B(eps_{l-1}, sg(c[l][k_l])) / s[l][k_l] )^2, beta inherited unchanged from the baseline config. No gradient flows into s.

ideas.title: Co-evolving per-code behavioural curvature field that sizes each RQ-VAE cell by the measured branching of its own successor set.

blocking_findings.correction: Implement the mechanism inside the executed quantizer: build the directed training-only transition matrix and carry item ids through the DataLoader batch; in VQLayer replace _distances/_indices with exp_0 of residual and codes, the mobius_add + artanh Poincare ground cost, the median-calibrated K=exp(-D/tau), the 3-iteration row-normalise -> (1-alpha)P + alpha*(B_bt @ P) -> column-normalise-to-q loop, argmax of P for j*(i) with a straight-through log_0(c_j*) pass-through, and the P-weighted Klein/Einstein code update; expose behaviour-off and Euclidean-cost switches in the same block.
blocking_findings.detail: There is no connected behaviour x curvature pathway. The quantizer is the unchanged Euclidean RecBole port: the ground cost is squared Euclidean (layers.py:98-104), the assignment is argmin or the old centre-rescaled Sinkhorn on the last level only (layers.py:106-113 together with layers.py:260-261), and the code "mean operator" is F.embedding plus KMeans init (layers.py:131-134, 139-146). No item ids ever reach the model: the dataset is TensorDataset(train_embeddings) (train_rqvae.py:261) and RQVAE.forward/get_indices accept only embeddings (model/model.py:26-36), so the proposal's B_bt (batch x batch directed-transition) block cannot even be constructed. The proposal's steps (1)-(6) appear nowhere: no Poincare ground cost, no exp_0 on the residual, no median-tau kernel, no 3-iteration diffusion with the alpha Markov step, no usage prior q, no Klein/Einstein weighted barycenter. The only curved code in the tree, model/utils.py:17-59 (artanh, proj_to_ball, mobius_add, expmap0, logmap0, poincare_distance) and HVectorQuantization at utils.py:162-329, is imported by nothing: model/__init__.py:3-4 imports only .layers and .model, layers.py imports no utils, and train_rqvae.py:37 does "from model import RQVAE". This is exactly the "inherited unused hyperbolic code" the scope contract excludes.
blocking_findings.reproduction: `grep -rn "poincare\|mobius\|artanh\|markov\|transition\|B_bt" train_rqvae.py model/layers.py model/model.py` returns no match; `grep -rn "utils" model/*.py` shows model/utils.py is never imported. Equivalently, make model.utils.poincare_distance raise AssertionError and run one step: training is unaffected, proving no executed path touches the curved helper.

blocking_findings.check: b) trainability (finite losses, gradients reach the intended parameters, switches change the assignment)
blocking_findings.correction: Add the coupled block with grad-carrying tensors (differentiable projected-Poincare distances from latents and codes, the diffused plan detached only where the proposal detaches it, straight-through log_0(c_j*) feeding the encoder gradient, P-weighted hyperbolic code step) and thread behaviour_on/curvature_on constants from the module into VQLayer so that flipping them provably changes the produced tokens.
blocking_findings.detail: The inherited Euclidean path is itself numerically sound and differentiable (recon MSE plus the straight-through commitment/codebook MSE at layers.py:132; where artanh exists it is clamped to +-(1-1e-10) at utils.py:18, so it cannot reach inf), but the proposal's coupled term and its parameters do not exist, so there is no coupled gradient to reach. No symbol such as use_behaviour, use_curvature, curvature_on, alpha, q or B_bt exists in the tree, so "both-on" is bit-identical to the Euclidean baseline: switching behaviour off, or replacing the curved cost by Euclidean, changes no assignment and no gradient. The behaviour-off / geometry-off / both-on comparisons required by the proposal are therefore all the same computation, and the claimed gradient into the hyperbolic code positions (the Einstein-midpoint update) is absent — a "gradient does not reach the parameter the proposal says it reaches" defect.
blocking_findings.reproduction: `grep -rn "use_behaviour\|use_curvature\|Einstein\|barycenter\|B_bt\|curvature" <tree>` returns nothing; there is no flag whose flip can change _indices, so a one-epoch smoke run only exercises the baseline quantizer and cannot show any on/off difference.

blocking_findings.correction: Implement the proposal inside the single assignment block: build the directed item-transition matrix from training sessions and index it by the batch item ids (train_rqvae.py:247-248 must feed a transition loader into the model); per level compute p_i=exp_0(r_i), the Poincare distance matrix, K=exp(-D/tau) with tau measured on the first batch, the three Sinkhorn sweeps with the Markov diffusion step and the measured q, argmax over P for the index, and the hyperbolic weighted barycenter codebook update with the plan weights. Remove or wire the dead utils helpers so that one path uses both signals.
blocking_findings.detail: The implementation is the unchanged baseline Euclidean RQ-VAE. Assignment is torch.argmin over ||r_i - c_j||^2 (layers.py:98-104, 113), or the original Euclidean Sinkhorn on centered Euclidean distances at the last level only (layers.py:81-96, 106-112). There is no directed transition matrix, no Markov diffusion P <- (1-alpha)P + alpha*(B_bt @ P), no Poincare ground cost, no exp/log maps, no curved quantization and no hyperbolic Klein/Einstein barycenter code anywhere. train_rqvae.py:247-248 reads train.parquet only to take unique "target" item ids; no session/sequence column is touched, so no training-only behaviour signal is computed at all. The hyperbolic functions in model/utils.py:17-59 and 162-329 are dead code: grep finds no reference outside utils.py, and neither model/__init__.py nor model/layers.py imports utils. This is exactly the prohibited "unused hyperbolic helper / behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer" case, except the helpers are not even imported.
blocking_findings.reproduction: grep -R "transition\|markov\|diffus\|Einstein\|Klein\|barycenter" over the tree returns only the unrelated EMA "alpha" at layers.py:196-197; grep -R "from .utils\|import utils" returns nothing; read layers.py:98-113 and observe argmin over Euclidean distances. Additionally, the existing Euclidean Sinkhorn is training-only and last-level only; the SID export calls get_indices(..., infer_use_sk=False) at train_rqvae.py:415-417, which reaches the argmin branch at layers.py:107-113.

blocking_findings.check: (b) trainability -- finite forward/backward, gradients reach intended parameters, coupled pathway changes SID/gradients when switched on and reverts when behaviour is off or curvature is Euclidean
blocking_findings.correction: Add explicit behaviour-on/off, geometry-on/off and both-on switches to the assignment block, with the behaviour-off arm using the identity diffusion and the geometry-off arm using Euclidean distance, and ensure each switch changes the plan/cost used both in the forward assignment and in the codebook update. The curved operations and transition lookup must sit on the live autograd path so their gradients reach the encoder/codebook as specified.
blocking_findings.detail: The baseline Euclidean path is differentiable and finite-checked (loss guard at train_rqvae.py:322-323), but the coupled pathway required by the proposal is absent. There is no behaviour switch, no geometry switch and no both-on/off wiring anywhere in the tree, so nothing can change SID assignment or gradients when "switched on", and nothing can revert when behaviour is off or the curve is replaced by Euclidean distance. The only hyperbolic ops (model/utils.py:162-329) are never instantiated or called, so they receive no gradient; the only trainable quantization parameters are the Euclidean nn.Embedding weights (layers.py:62), updated through the Euclidean quant_loss. There is therefore no coupled term whose gradient could reach the intended parameters.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Inspect the forward graph: layers.py:98-104 takes no transition-matrix argument and calls no expmap0/poincare_distance; grep for any switch/env/flag over behaviour or curvature returns nothing; model/utils.py is never imported, so its parameters never appear in model.parameters(). Switching the non-existent switches is impossible, so the required on/off SID comparison cannot be exercised.

blocking_findings.check: a) behaviour x geometry fidelity — is there ONE connected pathway that uses the training-only behaviour signal and the curved operation together?
blocking_findings.correction: Implement the specified block inside RQLayer/VQLayer (or a new quantizer class actually instantiated by RQVAE): build the training-only directed-transition matrix from the frozen stage0 train parquet, form the Poincare distance cost D_ij, run the T=3 diffused Sinkhorn sweeps P <- (1-alpha)P + alpha*(B_bt @ P) with row/column marginals, use argmax(P) for the SID token, and add the closed-form hyperbolic (Klein/Einstein) weighted barycenter codebook update with P detached, plus explicit behaviour_on/geometry_on switches threaded from the trainer config.
blocking_findings.detail: The implementation contains no behaviour signal at all. There is no directed-transition/co-consumption matrix, no B_bt, no Markov diffusion of the assignment plan, and no behaviour-derived weights anywhere in the tree (the only grep hits for the mechanism vocabulary are incidental `mlp` matches). The hyperbolic Poincare quantizer that does exist, HVectorQuantization/HResidualVectorQuantization in model/utils.py:162-276, is dead code: it is never imported by model/__init__.py (which imports only layers at lines 3-4) and the RQVAE wrapper builds layers.RQLayer (model/model.py:23), whose VQLayer uses Euclidean squared distance and Euclidean argmin/Sinkhorn. So the "curvature in the cost kernel" claim is not even connected to the trainer, and the "behaviour enters the assignment plan" claim has no implementation. There is exactly one connected computation and it contains neither half of the proposed coupling; the behaviour-off/geometry-off switches required by the scope contract do not exist.
blocking_findings.reproduction: `grep -rn "transition\|markov\|einstein\|klein\|B_bt" model/ train_rqvae.py` returns nothing mechanism-related; `python -c "import model; print(model.RQVAE.__module__)"` and reading model/model.py:23 plus model/layers.py:98-113 shows the trainer's quantizer is the Euclidean VQLayer; model/utils.py is imported by no module in the tree.

blocking_findings.check: b) trainability — real forward/backward, finite losses and gradients reaching the intended parameters, coupled pathway changing SID assignment/gradients and reverting when behaviour or curvature is switched off
blocking_findings.correction: Implement the coupled quantizer so that argmax(P) (differentiable through the straight-through path) and the detached-plan barycenter both live in the executed forward, register the curvature as a fixed constant or a parameter, and wire the three switches (behaviour on/off, geometry on/off, both) into the trainer config so the same single run uses the both-on branch while the off branches remain callable; guard Poincare distances with a norm clamp below 1 (e.g. clamp to 1-1e-5) before artanh and keep the existing NaN check.
blocking_findings.detail: The path that does run (Euclidean RQ-VAE) is numerically ordinary: the straight-through estimator at layers.py:133 and the MSE quant_loss at layers.py:132 give finite losses and gradients to the encoder/decoder and to the codebook. But the proposal's coupled pathway has no code in the executed graph, so there is no gradient that reaches a curvature parameter or a behaviour-conditioned assignment plan, and there is no dead term to point at either because the term was never written. Consequently the required switches cannot be exercised: switching behaviour off or replacing the Poincare kernel with Euclidean changes nothing, since neither exists in the forward pass. The claims in the proposal that the SID assignment is plan-based and that the codebook update is an Einstein midpoint are both unrealized (layers.py:113 uses argmin; layers.py:139-146 uses sklearn KMeans in Euclidean space). Note also that the dead model/utils.py sinkhorn (utils.py:139-159) is a different, non-diffused implementation from the specified one, so even importing it would not satisfy the proposal.
blocking_findings.reproduction: Read model/model.py:23 and follow self.rq into model/layers.py:283-290 -> layers.py:98-113; nothing in that chain is differentiable with respect to any behaviour or curvature input, and grep finds no switch flag (behaviour_on/geometry_on/euclidean) anywhere. Running the trainer would produce a plain Euclidean RQ-VAE training curve identical to the baseline, because that is literally the code being run.

per_scorer_objection.scoring_1: The "curvature" is a positive scalar gain on a Euclidean residual, so the whole mechanism is a per-prefix codebook rescale: for a fixed prefix, argmin_k ||lambda_p r - c_k|| = argmin_k ||r - c_k/lambda_p||. There is no exp/log map, no geodesic, no Mobius step; the number of codes per level is unchanged, so amplification only reallocates which existing codes are used, and the assignment is exactly reproducible by a Euclidean quantizer with a per-prefix code scale. A second, independent defect is that the stated geometry-off limit is arithmetically wrong: at c=0 the stated factor is 2/(1-0)=2, not the claimed 1.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_2: lambda_p enters only as a positive scalar gain on the residual and encode multiplies while decode divides, so the reconstructed item is unchanged and the only live effect is a per-node temperature on the next level's argmin; a per-node learnable gain g_p (one Euclidean scalar per node) is a matched control that reproduces this for every finite norm, and the proposal never argues what the functional form 2/(1-c||x||^2) adds beyond g_p.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_3: The "curved" step is a positive scalar gain applied to a Euclidean residual: argmin_j ||lambda_p r - c_j||^2 = argmin_j ||r - c_j/lambda_p||^2, so the whole mechanism is a per-node radial dilation of a Euclidean codebook, and the exact same numbers come out of a Euclidean radial gain g(||r||)=2/(1-c_p||r||^2). No exp/log map, no distance, no Mobius operation is evaluated, so nothing in the computation is hyperbolic rather than curved-looking.

Decompose the score: the first-order term in the operating regime is the behaviour gain 1/s_k, while the artanh warp contributes only O(||c||^2), so the curved part is a second-order correction on top of something a Euclidean per-prototype scale does directly. A separate numerical gap: a cell with B=0 gives s=0 and divides by zero in both the search and the commitment term, and the promised clamp bound is never stated.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_2: The statistic is measured one level off from where it is used: B[l][k] is how the items in cell (l,k) spread their successors over level-l sibling groups, but the remedy enlarges cell (l,k) itself, and a larger parent cell does not separate the successors - it absorbs more items, which raises B further; the risk list admits drift to a few huge cells but does not break the loop.
per_scorer_objection.scoring_3: Behaviour reaches the quantizer only through kappa[l][k], so the declared geometry-off arm - "keeps the behaviour weights but removes curvature" - has no implementable pathway: with curvature removed there is no place for B[l][k] to enter, and geometry-off is bit-identical to behaviour-off, so the three named switches are really two arms and the one run cannot separate the behaviour switch from the geometry switch. Secondary: each cell sets s[l][k] independently, with no volume budget (sum_k vol_k = const), so a uniform rise in B across codes multiplies every kappa and just rescales all distances - the field's contrast, not its level, carries the mechanism.

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc

papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. papers.title: HVQ-VAE: Variational auto-encoder with hyperbolic vector quantization

papers.abstract: The success of models operating on tokenized data has heightened the need for effective tokenization methods, particularly in vision and auditory tasks where inputs are naturally continuous. A common solution is to employ Vector Quantization (VQ) within VQ Variational Autoencoders (VQVAEs), transforming inputs into discrete tokens by clustering embeddings in Euclidean space. However, Euclidean embeddings not only suffer from inefficient packing and limited separation - due to their polynomial volume growth - but are also prone to codebook collapse, where only a small subset of codebook vectors are effectively utilized. To address these limitations, we introduce HyperVQ, a novel approach that formulates VQ as a hyperbolic Multinomial Logistic Regression (MLR) problem, leveraging the exponential volume growth in hyperbolic space to mitigate collapse and improve cluster separability. Additionally, HyperVQ represents codebook vectors as geometric representatives of hyperbolic decision hyperplanes, encouraging disentangled and robust latent representations. Our experiments demonstrate that HyperVQ matches traditional VQ in generative and reconstruction tasks, while surpassing it in disc
papers.title: HyperVQ: MLR-based Vector Quantization in Hyperbolic Space

papers.abstract: In the last few decades, the kernel method has been successfully used in the field of adaptive filtering to solve nonlinear problems. Mercer kernel is used to map data from input space to reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) by kernel adaptive filter (KAF). In regenerated kernel Hilbert spaces, the inner product can be easily calculated by computing the so-called kernel trick. The Kernel adaptive filtering algorithm is superior to common adaptive filtering algorithm in solving nonlinear problems and nonlinear channel equalization. For nonlinear problems, a robust kernel least inverse hyperbolic sine (KLIHS) algorithm is proposed by combining the kernel method with the inverse of hyperbolic sine function.The main disadvantage of KAF is that the radial-basis function (RBF) network grows with every new data sample, which increases the computational-complexity and requires more momories. The vector quantization (VQ) has been proposed to address this problem and has been successfully applied to the current kernel adaptive filtering algorithm. papers.abstract: We present a novel vector quantization (VQ) module for the two state-of-the-art long-range simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) algorithms. The VQ task in SLAM is generally performed using unsupervised methods. We provide an alternative approach trough embedding a semisupervised hyperbolic graph convolutional neural network (HGCN) in the VQ step of the SLAM processes. The SLAM platforms we have utilized for this purpose are fast appearance-based mapping (FABMAP) and oriented fast and rotated short (ORB), both of which rely on extracting the features of the captured images in their loop closure detection (LCD) module. For the first time, we have considered the space formed by these SURF features, robust image descriptors, as a graph, enabling us to apply an HGCN in the VQ section which results in an improved LCD performance. The HGCN vector quantizes the SURF feature space, leading to a bag-of-word (BoW) representation construction of the images. This representation is subsequently used to determine LCD accuracy and recall. Our approaches in this study are referred to as HGCN-FABMAP and HGCN-ORB. The main advantage of using HGCN in the LCD section is that it scales linearly
papers.title: Semisupervised Vector Quantization in Visual SLAM Using HGCN
The Deformation Quantizations of the Hyperbolic Plane

papers.abstract: Residual Vector Quantization turns continuous representations into discrete, multi-level token sequences. Yet most methods operate in Euclidean space, despite the coarse-to-fine structure of the resulting codes and the latent hierarchies present in many data domains. Hyperbolic geometry offers a natural alternative for hierarchical representations, but naive hyperbolic extensions introduce geometric inconsistencies: non-associative hyperbolic addition prevents consistent residual aggregation, while standard straight-through gradient estimation ignores the geometry of the latent space. We propose a geometry-aware hyperbolic residual quantization that addresses these issues in both the forward and backward passes. In the forward pass, Hyperbolic Residual Aggregation restores the telescoping behavior of residual quantization on the Poincare ball. In the backward pass, a discounted Hyperbolic Straight-Through Estimator routes the reconstruction gradient through the quantizer as a single geometric block, avoiding unstable recursive gradient transport across residual stages. papers.title: Geometry-Aware Hyperbolic Residual-Quantized Variational Autoencoders

papers.abstract: We develop a cannonical quantization for massive vector fields on a globally hyperbolic Lorentzian manifold.
papers.title: Quantization of massive vector fields in curved space–time

papers.abstract: Most high-performance block-coding systems for image compression, such as JPEG, have been designed for software or dedicated digital hardware implementations where the data are already assumed to be available in digital format. In modern CMOS photosensors, smart-pixel technologies have allowed the realization of basic signal processing tasks at the pixel level, in analog format before analog-to-digital (A/D) conversion. The elimination of A/D converters and implementation of block-coding directly over analog blocks of pixels in such sensors can be attractive both in terms of area savings and power consumption. The design of block encoders, under the strong hardware constraints that derive from the A/D converter removal, has been investigated in this paper. We present a comparison of three systems in terms of rate, distortion and complexity, and present a numerical simulation analysis of their sensitivity to implementation errors. The conclusion of the analysis is that linear-transform coding vector quantizers outperform full-search vector quantizers and warping hyperbolic-tangent neural networks, in terms of performance, complexity and robustness, for a CMOS imaging sensor implemen
papers.title: Sensitivity analysis of low-complexity vector quantizers for focal-plane image compression

papers.abstract: Vector quantization is a technique in machine learning that discretizes continuous representations into a set of discrete vectors. It is widely employed in tokenizing data representations for large language models, diffusion models, and other generative models. Despite its prevalence, the characteristics and behaviors of vector quantization in generative models remain largely underexplored. In this study, we investigate representation collapse in vector quantization - a critical degradation where codebook tokens or latent embeddings lose their discriminative power by converging to a limited subset of values. This collapse fundamentally compromises the model's ability to capture diverse data patterns. By leveraging both synthetic and real datasets, we identify the severity of each type of collapses and triggering conditions. Our analysis reveals that restricted initialization and limited encoder capacity result in tokens collapse and embeddings collapse. Building on these findings, we propose potential solutions aimed at mitigating each collapse. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive study examining representation collapsing problems in vector quantization.
papers.title: Representation Collapsing Problems in Vector Quantization

papers.abstract: Machine learning algorithms have been shown to be highly effective in solving optimization problems in a wide range of applications. Such algorithms typically use gradient descent with backpropagation and the chain rule. Hence, the backpropagation fails if intermediate gradients are zero for some functions in the computational graph, because it causes the gradients to collapse when multiplying with zero. Vector quantization is one of those challenging functions for machine learning algorithms, since it is a piece-wise constant function and its gradient is zero almost everywhere. A typical solution is to apply the straight through estimator which simply copies the gradients over the vector quantization function in the backpropagation. Other solutions are based on smooth or stochastic approximation. This study proposes a vector quantization technique called NSVQ, which approximates the vector quantization behavior by substituting a multiplicative noise so that it can be used for machine learning problems. Specifically, the vector quantization error is replaced by product of the original error and a normalized noise vector, the samples of which are drawn from a zero-mean, unit-varianc
papers.title: NSVQ: Noise Substitution in Vector Quantization for Machine Learning

findings.detail: There is no connected behaviour x curvature pathway. The quantizer is the unchanged Euclidean RecBole port: the ground cost is squared Euclidean (layers.py:98-104), the assignment is argmin or the old centre-rescaled Sinkhorn on the last level only (layers.py:106-113 together with layers.py:260-261), and the code "mean operator" is F.embedding plus KMeans init (layers.py:131-134, 139-146). The proposal's steps (1)-(6) appear nowhere: no Poincare ground cost, no exp_0 on the residual, no median-tau kernel, no 3-iteration diffusion with the alpha Markov step, no usage prior q, no Klein/Einstein weighted barycenter. The only curved code in the tree, model/utils.py:17-59 (artanh, proj_to_ball, mobius_add, expmap0, logmap0, poincare_distance) and HVectorQuantization at utils.py:162-329, is imported by nothing: model/__init__.py:3-4 imports only .layers and .model, layers.py imports no utils, and train_rqvae.py:37 does "from model import RQVAE". findings.detail: There is no behaviour switch and no curvature switch anywhere in the code, so the required comparison is not merely untested — it is unrepresentable. `_indices` is unconditionally `argmin` (levels 0 and 1, where `sk_epsilon` is forced to -1.0 by model/layers.py:260-261) or Euclidean-Sinkhorn `argmax` (level 2). Consequently switching "behaviour off" is a no-op and "geometry off" is a no-op: every candidate configuration produces the identical assignment and identical gradients, because the transition signal and the curved operation are never in the computation. The only differentiable curvature code in the tree, model/utils.py:260-263, is dead and, if wired in, would be wrong: `x_q` there is a Euclidean `codebook.index_select` row (line 258) pushed through `logmap0` (line 265) and compared against the un-mapped Euclidean `latent` (line 266), while the Poincare-mapped `x_exp`/`cb_exp` from lines 256-257 are computed and discarded, so the commitment/codebook distances would mix a ball point with a flat point. Separately, model/utils.py:36 `den.clamp_min(_eps(den))` clamps with the dtype epsilon of the denominator rather than a magnitude-relative floor, and `poincare_distance` at line 58 clamps the Mobius norm at eps before `artanh`, so the injected value is fine but the `mobius_add` denominator can go to eps=1.19e-7 for ball-near-boundary points and blow the gradient up; that hazard must not be carried into the live path.
findings.reproduction: Read model/layers.py:107 — the condition is `(self.training and self.use_sk) or (self.use_sk and infer_use_sk)`, and `use_sk` derives only from `sk_epsilon > 0 and sk_iters > 0` (model/layers.py:59); there is no flag whose value changes the distance function or adds a transition term. `grep -rn "use_curvature\|use_behaviour\|curvature\|transition" <tree> --include=*.py` returns nothing, so no ablation switch exists to flip.

findings.check: c) integration — trainer entry point, frozen data path, valid and correctly indexed SID export, writes only into its own result directory, distributed launcher including the SINGLE_GPU_ENV = "GENREC_SINGLE_GPU" single-card branch
findings.correction:
Restore the single-card branch, e.g. at the top of `_launch_via_torchrun`: if `os.environ.get(SINGLE_GPU_ENV) == "1"` (with `SINGLE_GPU_ENV = "GENREC_SINGLE_GPU"` defined as a module constant), set `os.environ["CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES"]` to the chosen single device and fall through to `main()` with `world_size = 1` instead of forking four ranks, and have `main()` respect `BATCH_SIZE_PER_RANK` scaled to the total batch the contract specifies for one card.

Note, not a defect: `RESULT_DIR` living under `results/stage2_RQ-VAE/<arm>/` is required, and the SID export itself is sound — `_extend_collisions` (train_rqvae.py:195-208) offsets the fourth token by `cumsum([0,256,256,256])[-1] = 768` plus an occurrence index inside each prefix group, the uniqueness assertion at line 422 is correct, and `item_sids.json` is keyed by the `all_embeddings` row index produced by `get_indices` over the full item set, so the indexing is consistent with the frozen Stage 3 reader. The data path (train_rqvae.py:61-62, `stage1_GeneEmbedding/output/sentence_t5.npy` and `results/stage0_build_parquet/train.parquet`, with `target` ids validated against the embedding rows at lines 248-250) is the frozen one. The four-card DDP path, the final-epoch-only checkpoint (lines 386-407) and the `infer_use_sk=False` export with `_skip_ddp_reduce` (lines 411-420) are consistent with the frozen protocol.
findings.detail: The launcher has no branch reading `SINGLE_GPU_ENV = "GENREC_SINGLE_GPU"`. `_launch_via_torchrun` returns early only when `RANK` is already set (line 438), otherwise it unconditionally calls `stage2_launcher.launch(..., world_size=int(_LAUNCHER["nproc"]))` with `nproc = 4` and `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="0,1,2,3"` (lines 103, 106, 442). On a single-card host this requests four workers that cannot be placed, so the entry point cannot run there at all; the four-card path is the only one implemented. scores.counterexample: lambda_p(0)=2/(1-0)=2 for every c_p, so the declared geometry-off limit c->0 gives lambda=2, not lambda=1: the "plain RQ sum" control is actually the baseline with every residual and codebook scaled by two, i.e. it changes all assignments and differs from the baseline by more than the intended switch. Worse, for c_p=10 and ||x||=0.4 (allowed, since z=tanh(.)*(1-1e-6)), 1-c_p||x||^2 = 1-1.6 = -0.6 and lambda = -3.33, so the residual is sign-flipped with a pole at ||x||=1/sqrt(c_p)=0.316.
scores.objection: The "curved" step is a positive scalar gain applied to a Euclidean residual: argmin_j ||lambda_p r - c_j||^2 = argmin_j ||r - c_j/lambda_p||^2, so the whole mechanism is a per-node radial dilation of a Euclidean codebook, and the exact same numbers come out of a Euclidean radial gain g(||r||)=2/(1-c_p||r||^2). No exp/log map, no distance, no Mobius operation is evaluated, so nothing in the computation is hyperbolic rather than curved-looking.
scores.rationale: behaviour=3 because the fanout heterogeneity itself is strongly measured (E5: top-1 successor mass 0.4375 in the lowest quintile against 0.0543 in the highest, support 2.77 vs 44.3, 4895 items in bin 1;
