E12 is truncated mid-sentence at "the conformal approximatio[n]", so whether a genuine distance term exists for the assignment score is UNKNOWN and the bounded check is reading the full SPEC EQUATIONS block. novelty=2: it is a routine variation of the per-node/per-branch curvature family already exercised in the ledger, differing by where the scalar is applied. downstream=3: the affected assignment and the expected direction are named, but the radial-gain argument says a larger lambda also shrinks the radius the fixed 256 codes can cover (the codebook supports |c| <= C, so effective radius in r-space is C/lambda), so hubs get finer cells and simultaneously lose reach, and the residual handed to level l+1 is already scaled by lambda_l, compounding to lambda1*lambda2*lambda3 <= 1000 in the worst case the proposal itself flags. falsifiability=3: the switches exist and the target 0.065 plus the two diagnostics (per-level entropy in the top fanout quartile, prefix-conditional next-code accuracy) are stated, but the geometry-off arm is arithmetically wrong as written and there is no sentence on what would refute the mechanism. implementability=3: the per-level multiply/divide inverts exactly in the no-quantization-error case and the cost is genuinely under a few percent, but the lambda pole and sign flip require a norm clamp that the visible spec does not state, and decode must divide by the product of all lambda along the prefix. exploration=2: a small variation of a family whose measured negatives are already in E6. Overall uncertainty is concentrated in the truncated spec: if E12/E13 do contain a real Mobius/distance assignment term, geometry_necessity could move to 3, but the encode/decode residual multiply described in the CHANGE field is a dilation either way.
scores.scope_reason: it names a training-only signal (popularity-adjusted directed successor fanout per prefix node, E1/E2), a curved operation (Poincare conformal factor with per-node negative curvature, E12) that enters the residual recursion at every level (E13), a single pathway where the curvature multiplies the residual, and three switches (USE_BEHAVIOUR, USE_HYPERBOLIC, both-on); nothing is missing for admission. The defect is geometric substance, not scope.

scores.counterexample: Take a batch of 1023 items drawn uniformly without session grouping. The expected number of rows with at least one in-batch successor is 1023*(1-(1-0.0417)^5.4526) ~ 215, and those rows get their mass mixed with a neighbour's column preferences by one (1-alpha) weight; for the remaining ~808 rows B_bt P = P exactly, so their argmax is the unmodified curved-Sinkhorn argmax. Scaling check on the cost: the proposal budgets "5-8 MFLOPs" for 9 (B x B)@(B x K) products, which requires nnz(B_bt) ~ 5.45*1023 = 5600 (giving 5600*256 = 1.43M per product); a dense B_bt would be 1023*1023*256 = 2.7e8 per product, a 190x error, so the budget only closes if the operator is kept explicitly sparse.
scores.objection: The Markov step is specified on the batch (B_bt @ P) while the transition matrix is global, and at the frozen batch size the operator is nearly the identity: with 24556 items and batches of 1023, the probability that a given training successor of item i is also in i's batch is 1023/24556 = 0.0417, so even at the measured mean out-degree 5.4526 (E10) the expected in-batch successor mass per row is at most 1-(1-0.0417)^5.45 = 0.21 and in practice far less once session locality is accounted for. With alpha<1 the T=3 loop then reduces to plain curved Sinkhorn plus a small neighbour ripple, and the behaviour switch is nearly inert while the curvature switch carries the whole run - the single run then tests geometry, not coupling.
scores.rationale: behaviour=4: this is the only proposal of the three whose named behavioural problem is measured on the SIDs themselves - E11 reports same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 against a permuted null 0.067 for the existing baseline SIDs, which is exactly "consecutive items land on codes with unrelated prefixes" - on top of E10 (118315 edges, mean out-degree 5.4526, explicit coverage note that the count is over sampled users) and E9 (positive shares a successor cohort 0.9291 vs 0.8871; profile entropy 1.65 nats over 7.5 cohorts, so the transition profile is not degenerate); the reason it is not a 5 is that the absolute prefix effect is small (9.07% vs 6.7%) and E11's own coverage is not shown in the bundle, so support is auditable but thin. geometry=3: Poincare distance, exp/log and the Einstein midpoint are genuine curved computations and the level-1 exp_0 is monotone in ||r||, so the curvature only bites through code-code Mobius geometry and boundary saturation; the proposal argues the switches are coupled but never specifies the matched Euclidean counterpart (Euclidean-distance RBF kernel plus Euclidean weighted mean) nor rules out the cancellation that the entropic kernel exp(-D/tau) is a monotone function of D and therefore close to a Euclidean RBF on the same points. novelty=3: moving the assignment plan itself with a diffused OT plan plus a hyperbolic barycenter is not in the ledger (E6 lists geodesic rank matching, shells, cones, tangent residuals, per-branch curvature, entropy variants) and is a distinct computation, but the argument is against our own ledger only and no external prior art is traced. downstream=4: the chain is specific (plan argmax -> code -> prefix; barycenter -> codebook), the expected direction is named for three observables - prefix hit-rate up, conditional code entropy down, recall above 0.065 - and the proposal states the discriminating reading (a rises while c does not => decorative structure). falsifiability=3: three arms are described but not enumerated as flags, "both off" is Sinkhorn-with-T=3 rather than the Euclidean argmin baseline, and the alpha value lives in a SAFEGUARDS section that is truncated, so the arms cannot be certified as differing in exactly one switch. implementability=3: the equations are complete enough to code, the straight-through path and the norm clamp are given, the cost is affordable under a sparse operator; but a code that draws zero plan mass has no defined Einstein midpoint, tau frozen from the first forward batch is a single-batch measurement, and the dense-vs-sparse discrepancy above is an unnamed risk. exploration=4: it is a substantially different mechanism (the assignment plan, not the latent, the loss or the rank order) and a negative result would be informative because it would say that behaviour-coupled assignment does not survive into the generator even when prefix structure improves.
scores.scope_reason: behaviour is the popularity-adjusted directed transition matrix restricted to training sessions (E1/E2, row-stochastic, sqrt(deg_out*deg_in) normalisation); geometry is an explicit curved computation (origin exp map, Mobius addition, Poincare distance as the Sinkhorn ground cost, Klein/Einstein weighted barycenter as the codebook operator, E12/E13); both act inside the same assignment block so removing either changes the plan, the argument or the code means. All five clauses hold.

scores.counterexample: Let all K cells at level l have the same branching B. Then q[m] is flat, H=log K, B_eff=K for every k, s_new is a single scalar for the whole level, and d_B(eps,c)/s is an ordinary constant-curvature quantizer - the "field" is a global scale and the mechanism is idle. The construction is reachable rather than pathological: E8 shows that at K=256 the first level already keeps only 0.0822 of canonical pairs co-clustered, so level-1 cells are numerous and their branch counts are pooled over few transitions each, which pushes B[l][k] toward a common value exactly where the field must discriminate.
scores.objection: Behaviour reaches the quantizer only through kappa[l][k], so the declared geometry-off arm - "keeps the behaviour weights but removes curvature" - has no implementable pathway: with curvature removed there is no place for B[l][k] to enter, and geometry-off is bit-identical to behaviour-off, so the three named switches are really two arms and the one run cannot separate the behaviour switch from the geometry switch. Secondary: each cell sets s[l][k] independently, with no volume budget (sum_k vol_k = const), so a uniform rise in B across codes multiplies every kappa and just rescales all distances - the field's contrast, not its level, carries the mechanism.
scores.rationale: behaviour=3: E5 measures the branching heterogeneity the mechanism consumes very strongly (support 2.77 -> 44.3 distinct successors, top-1 mass 0.4375 -> 0.0543, Spearman(entropy, top-1) -0.973, 4895 items in the lowest bin) and E10 supplies the transition base (118315 edges, mean out-degree 5.4526), so the signal exists; but the proposal's premise that "prefix entropy is limited by curvature budget" is contradicted where it can be checked, because E8 puts the ceiling at first-level capacity (K=256 -> 0.0822 co-cluster share vs 0.0129 negatives, K=16 -> 0.3106) and E6 has every curvature-flavoured arm at 0.0467-0.0550 against Euclidean 0.0621-0.0636, so the statistic is strong while the SID hypothesis that follows from it is not. geometry=3: the arithmetic is internally correct - s = sqrt(kappa) = log(1+B)/((d-1)R) is exactly the inverse-radius scale of curvature -kappa because a hyperbolic ball of radius R in d dimensions has log-volume ~ (d-1)R sqrt(kappa), and dividing the unit-ball distance by sqrt(kappa) is the metric of curvature -kappa, so this is not a dimensional mismatch or a cancellation; what is missing is that the executed operation is a per-code scalar division that a per-code temperature in a weighted Euclidean nearest-neighbour rule reproduces, and no matched Euclidean control is specified, so the only genuinely non-Euclidean content is the exponential volume argument and that is not argued against a control. novelty=3: per-code and refreshed rather than global and static is a distinct computation from the ledger's global curvature and shells, and the self-consistency loop is new here, but no external prior art is traced and per-branch curvature already sits in the ledger family. downstream=4: the affected assignment (level-l cell boundaries, hence the prefix) and the expected direction of three observables are named - positive Spearman between |A_k| and B_k, falling H(next code | level-0 code), recall above 0.065 - and the failure reading is explicit. falsifiability=3: the switches exist and the criterion is stated, but the geometry-off arm is not implementable as described (see objection), so the arms are two rather than three matched controls. implementability=4: equations, refresh epochs {1,2,4,...,2048} derived from the 3000-epoch budget, cumulative-mean damping with no tuned decay, tanh*(1-1e-6) guarding the atanh, explicit clamping of s, no gradient into s, L*K = 1024 extra floats and roughly +1.05M scalar ops per step; the remaining risks are named, and the only unnamed one is the un-normalised volume budget. exploration=3: a different failure mode from the family (a self-consistent curvature field that can drift or go flat) whose negative would still be informative, but it lives in the same curvature-of-prefix family that E6 has already measured below the Euclidean arms. The dimension I cannot fully ground is the level-1 branch-count pooling: E5 reports global successor stratification, not per-cell B[l][k] at K=256, and the bounded check that would resolve it is one pass over the training transitions counting distinct successor cells per level-1 code.
scores.scope_reason: behaviour is the effective number of distinct successor code-groups B[l][k] of each current SID cell, built from consecutive training-session pairs only (E1/E2, E3); geometry is per-code negative curvature entering as the curvature-rescaled Poincare distance d_B(eps,c)/sqrt(kappa) in both the nearest-code search and the commitment term, with the Mobius residual chain (E12/E13); the two are one pathway (behaviour sets kappa, kappa sets cell size, the partition re-measures behaviour) so removing either changes the core computation. All five clauses hold.
